I judged the declared Risk 3 against group_unix.go. ownGroup sets Setpgid and a Cancel that sends SIGKILL to -pid, with ESRCH mapped to os.ErrProcessDone. I found no defect. Cancel runs only after the process has started, so cmd.Process is set. The group id is the leader's pid, and the process is already reaped whenever Cancel is skipped, so there is no pid-reuse hazard.

The group is opt-in. Only review_stop_hook.go calls WithProcessGroup, and New() leaves it off, which TestProcessGroupIsOptIn checks. Run and outputIn both call ownGroup only when the option is set. The group_other.go no-op leaves the kill unchanged on non-Unix builds. The only behaviour change is that a Ctrl-C at a terminal no longer reaches the evidence script. The doc comment states this and the hook is not interactive, so I do not count it as a defect.

The os.Stat check in evidencesh.Classified only short-circuits on fs.ErrNotExist. It names the store as not deployed and does not run it. Any other stat error goes on to the run. The tests cover the error text, that it wraps fs.ErrNotExist, and that the runner is not called.

review.ShortName is name[:min(len(name), 12)], so it cannot panic on a short name. Candidate.Short still returns "" for a head under 12 characters. The two removed copies, app.short and head12, are replaced at their call sites in stop.go and review_stop_hook.go.
The literal-12 lint test and the prose-based text tests only change test code. I found no user-impacting problem in them.
The README and CHANGELOG edits match the new behaviour and are pinned by the new docs tests.
